## Active

### D-009 — The profile avatar shows initials only, never a photo

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · active_

A photo or upload was considered and dropped: the avatar is initials derived from the `party.person`
name, falling back to the username and then the email address, and finally to the generic `pi-user`
icon when none of them exists. Initials avoid image storage, upload validation and a second avatar
endpoint, and the fallback chain means a user without any name data still gets a coherent avatar
instead of an empty button.

### D-010 — The profile opens as a portal tab from the account menu

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · active_

The profile is reached as a tab in the portal rather than as a separate page route: the AccountMenu
calls `openTab`, wired through a new `IPortalConfig.profile = {page, get}` entry. Keeping it a tab
means the profile lives inside the same portal layout (menubar, tabs, theming) as the rest of the
application and needs no routing changes.

### D-011 — Profile config nests inside the inner portal key, login stays a sibling

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · active_

`profile` must live INSIDE the inner `ui.portal.portal.{...}` block so that `portalConfigGet` /
`this.config.portal` carries it to the AccountMenu. `login` and `google` must stay SIBLINGS of that
inner `portal` key, because `App` reads them from the portal component's config; nesting them inside
the inner `portal` breaks the Register and Google buttons. The two placements look interchangeable
and are not.

### D-012 — Profile page JSX lives in src/pages so tap never loads a .tsx

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · active_

The profile page component sits in `core/blong-browser/src/pages/`, outside the well-known browser
layer folders, and is imported lazily. The reason is the Node tap runner: it loads the browser
layers and cannot load `.tsx`, so a page placed in `./browser` breaks `index.test.ts`. Living in
`src/pages` means only Vite ever bundles it.

### D-013 — A Playwright test must request the portal fixture

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · active_

A test that only destructures `{page}` never triggers the `portal` fixture, so the page stays
`about:blank` and the failure looks like an application bug. The fixture is what does the `goto` and
the login, so any test that needs a rendered app has to ask for `portal` explicitly.

### D-014 — The UI applies the login language in the auth handlers

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · active_

`authLogin` and `authSessionGet` call `setLanguage(profile.language)` as soon as the profile
arrives, instead of each page doing it on mount. Suites therefore need no per-page wiring, and a
reload that restores the session re-applies the stored preference through the same path.

### D-015 — Translations are registered per language in appStore

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · active_

`setTranslationsByLanguage` registers one dictionary per language and `setLanguage` swaps the active
`translations` table only when dictionaries are registered; an empty `translationsByLanguage` means
the legacy behaviour, so existing tests and stories that call `setTranslations` together with
`setLanguage` are unaffected. Registration order against `setLanguage` does not matter, because both
re-apply.

### D-016 — Each suite owns its translation dictionaries via portal.translations

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · active_

Translation dictionaries are suite configuration rather than framework data: blong-access declares
`portal.translations` as `{en: {}, bg: {...}}`, and an empty English dictionary means English
strings fall back to the key itself. Translation keys ARE the English strings, following the
existing `tr()`/`useText` convention, so no separate key catalogue had to be invented.

### D-017 — The Bulgarian PrimeReact locale ships inside blong-browser

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · active_

`bgLocale` lives in `core/blong-browser/src/primereact/locales.ts` and is included in
`DEFAULT_THEME.languages`, so `setLanguage('bg')` cannot crash an app with PrimeReact's "navigation
option not found" error. It is registered always and activated only when the language is `bg`. The
alternative — per-app `theme.languages` through the portal config — was rejected as more plumbing
for no benefit, since the locale data is framework-agnostic.

### D-018 — Tabs get min-height: 0 so a portal page cannot grow past the viewport

> _2026-07-09 · core/blong-browser · active_

`.p-tabview`, `.p-tabview .p-tabview-panels` and `.p-tabview .p-tabview-panel` in `Portal.css`
gained `min-height: 0`, so a tab fills the portal body and never grows beyond the viewport — a
573-row table used to stretch the whole page to roughly 18,000 px. This is global: any page that
previously relied on growing beyond the viewport now scrolls internally, which was a bug rather than
a feature. If a non-commander page's Playwright baseline shifts, regenerate it.

### D-033 — The menubar language switch is client-side and not persisted

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · active_

The switcher calls `appStore.setLanguage` only; it does NOT persist the choice to the user's profile
— that is the profile page's `preferredLanguage` edit. On the next login the stored preference wins,
so the switcher is deliberately a session-level, ad-hoc control rather than a second place that
writes preferences.

### D-034 — A LanguageSwitcher dropdown sits left of the account menu

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · active_

`core/blong-browser/src/components/LanguageSwitcher/` renders a compact `Dropdown` (the
blong-browser wrapper) showing the current language; it is mounted in `App.tsx`'s `menubarEnd`, to
the LEFT of `<AccountMenu />`, and hides itself when fewer than two languages are available.

### D-035 — The switcher's language list comes from portal.languages

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · active_

`portal.languages: Array<{value, label}>` was added to `IPortalConfig` AND `IBlongPortalConfig`, and
falls back to the keys of `portal.translations`, so any app with translations gets a switcher
without extra configuration. A prop override is supported for tests.

### D-036 — New portal config fields must be added to IPortalConfig too

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · active_

The store's `portalConfig` is typed as `IPortalConfig` (`src/types/portal.ts`), NOT
`IBlongPortalConfig`, so a new portal config field — here `languages` and `translations` — has to be
added to `IPortalConfig` as well or tsc fails in the components that read the store.

### D-037 — Adding the switcher invalidates every menubar baseline

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · active_

The switcher changes the menubar in every suite that shows one, so ALL Playwright baselines
containing the menubar had to be re-captured — blong-access's full suite was refreshed with
`--update-snapshots=all`. Treat a new menubar widget as a repository-wide baseline change, not a
local one.

### D-038 — Querying a PrimeReact Dropdown means textContent, not role

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · active_

In vitest the dropdown opens with `userEvent.click` on the dropdown root (mousedown toggles the
panel) and its options render as `.p-dropdown-item` in a body portal, so query them by `textContent`
— the `role="option"` name matcher is unreliable there. In Playwright, assert the current selection
on `.p-dropdown-label`, because the root element's text also contains the hidden input value (for
example "EnglishEnglish").

### D-039 — Master-detail models nest the child arrays inside the master object

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-browser · active_

`IModelSpec.details` produces NESTED array properties on the master object schema
(`{invoice: {..., line: [...]}}`), chosen over the kopi override's top-level-sibling shape
`{invoice: {...}, lines: [...]}`. Nesting matches the existing dotted-path form payload and needs no
manual override.

### D-040 — Playwright element waits time out after five seconds

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-browser · active_

`BLONG_ELEMENT_TIMEOUT = 5_000` — the upper end of the plan's 3-5 second range — was picked to keep
some CI headroom while still failing fast compared with the 30-second default.

### D-078 — Glass glare is placed per lane, anchored on each lane's top card

> _2026-09-06 · core/blong-browser · active_

The final glass-glare design: the editor re-lays itself between one column (narrow) and two card
columns (wide, beyond about 1200 px), plus a full-width header toolbar and a right Form Inspector
rail, and a single straight glare edge can only cross one vertical lane. So the left lane (header
toolbar plus the left-most card column) shares ONE straight edge, the right card column gets its own
parallel edge because it cannot share the full-width header line, and the Form Inspector is
independent with a fixed `--glare-shift` of 50% ("starting at the middle"). A lane's anchor is its
top-most CARD rather than the header, at `ANCHOR_FRACTION` 0.5 — anchoring on the wide header
stretches and over-lights the narrow cards. `glassReflection.ts` clusters non-header cards by
centre-x (`COLUMN_GAP` 120 px), the header joins `columns[0]`, and `updateGlassReflections` re-runs
on resize so the lanes follow reflow. Verified live at 1500 px by edge constants: left lane toolbar
23.2 / edit 50 / morphology 35.3 / links 26.6 (C=340.7), right lane taxonomy 50 / reproduction 42.6
/ habitat 36.3 (C=944), inspector 50; in single-column mode header 40.5 / edit 50 through habitat
15.8 all sit on one line.

### D-079 — Playwright ports are derived from the package's rush.json index

> _2026-09-07 · core/blong-browser · active_

Realms running Playwright under parallel `rush ci-test` all defaulted to 8080/5173 and collided with
"http://localhost:8080 is already used". Hand-written unique ports per realm (9001/9101 through
9086/9186) were the first fix but were brittle and easy to forget when a realm was added. The final
design (user-chosen option 1) has `defineBlongConfig`
(`core/blong-browser/src/playwright/config.ts`) derive a per-package port pair from the package's
index in `rush.json` (`backend = 9000 + index`, `frontend = backend + 100`), applied ONLY in CI,
with a local fallback to 8080/5173 so a single local run reuses the running dev server. Priority:
explicit `backendPort`/`frontendPort` option, then
`PLAYWRIGHT_BACKEND_PORT`/`PLAYWRIGHT_FRONTEND_PORT`, then the derived pair in CI, then 8080/5173
locally — using `stripJsoncComments` (rush.json is JSONC) and `findUp` helpers. The hand-written
ports were removed from all seven realm `playwright.config.ts` files, now kopi 9014/9114, commander
9015/9115, marine 9033/9133, access 9035/9135, gateway 9037/9137, party 9038/9138 and suite
9040/9140, verified numerically and by a commander run on both paths. Simulating CI locally is
`CI=1 PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_INSTALL=1`, because `blong-dev playwright` otherwise runs
`playwright install --with-deps` and prompts for sudo; real CI sets `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_INSTALL: '1'`
and pre-installs browsers. Out of scope: `blong-graph/playwright.config.{js,ts}` is a standalone
config with its own `test:server` on port 3000, and the gitignored
`common/deploy/core/blong-kopi/playwright.config.ts` still hardcodes 9003/9103.

### D-080 — The theme switcher lists families, with glass and wood standalone

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-browser · active_

The App menubar gained a theme switcher built as one dropdown entry per PrimeReact theme FAMILY (16
families = 32 folders) plus 24 single-variant themes and the blong `glass`/`wood` variants — 42
entries — with a sun/moon light/dark toggle that appears only when the selected option has BOTH
variants. Glass and Wood are standalone (user-chosen): dark base, no light/dark toggle, and their
CSS is dark-only, layered over the config default folder
(`PRIMEREACT_PALETTE_THEMES[type][palette]`). State lives in `appStore.theme`
(`{themeId?, palette?}` plus `setTheme`) and persists to `localStorage['blong.theme']` (read at
store creation, guarded by `typeof localStorage`); the `<Theme>` provider merges it over the
`IThemeConfig` prop so an explicit selection outranks config. `IThemeConfig.switcher?: boolean`
(default true) makes `ThemeSwitcher` return `null`, exposed through the new `useTheme()` context
(`IThemeContextValue`), and the new `IThemeConfig.name?: string` accepts a theme-option id
(`lara-blue`, `glass`) or a PrimeReact folder (`lara-dark-blue`), overriding the legacy `type` plus
`palette` mapping while `type` stays font-size only. CSS is swapped with `?inline` plus a single
`<style id="blong-prime-theme">` (`themeRegistry.ts` `THEME_LOADERS`), which also fixed a latent
bug: side-effect dynamic imports are never re-injected, so revisiting a theme kept losing to a
later-loaded one — exactly one theme is active now, verified by confirming that `?inline` returns
the full 178,538-character vela-blue CSS with a throwaway Vite build. Menubar order is
`<ThemeSwitcher />`, then `<LanguageSwitcher />`, then `<AccountMenu />`; Storybook's `withDispatch`
resets the theme selection per story so `parameters.theme` wins; and files containing theme names
carry a file-local spelling-checker disable comment instead of global dictionary changes. Verified:
36 targeted tests plus the full blong-browser suite at 450 passed, with only the pre-existing
`Editor.test.tsx` failing on `@feasibleone/marine-data`.

### D-142 — A menubar regression is fixed in CSS, not by refreshing baselines

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-browser · active_

Two independent causes made every `blong-kopi` Playwright test fail after the wood theme commit: the
`?inline` PrimeReact theme CSS was served as raw `text/css`, so the browser refused the module
script and no theme was applied, and `.p-menubar-end` is a block box in PrimeReact, so the newly
added `ThemeSwitcher` plus the account menu stacked into two rows and grew the menubar from 49px to
about 76px, shifting all page content. Both were fixed in `blong-browser` instead of running
`playwright --update-snapshots`: `src/vite.ts` adds `primereact` to `server.fs.allow`, because
Vite's dev fs guard runs the allow-list check on query-bearing requests so a module-graph-only path
is served raw rather than transformed, and `src/components/Portal/Portal.css` makes `.p-menubar-end`
a flex row. The reasoning is that the menubar growth is a genuine layout regression, not an intended
design change: restoring the 49px height returns the diff to under 1%, so the committed baselines
stay valid. Reconsider, meaning update the baselines, only if the taller menubar is actually wanted.

### D-143 — Refreshing baselines on purpose needs --update-snapshots=all

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-browser · active_

`--update-snapshots` with Playwright's default mode `changed` is a no-op when the comparison passes:
it only rewrites failing snapshots. The theme switcher's footprint of about 0.3% is under
`maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01`, so nothing was rewritten by the first attempt. A deliberate refresh needs
`--update-snapshots=all`, run here as
`node_modules/.bin/blong-dev playwright --update-snapshots=all`.

### D-144 — Most refreshed baselines differ because they predate the folder move

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-browser · active_

The refresh rewrote 198 baselines in 6 packages: access 62, marine 38, party 38, gateway 28,
commander 19, kopi 13; plain runs afterwards passed (commander 10, kopi 4, marine 14, access 21 plus
3 flaky, party 16, gateway 12). 91 of the 198 differ only in the menubar, where the new switcher
sits, and 107 differ elsewhere as well because those baselines are older than the
`fix: split core to folders` move — the move re-pathed them without regenerating content, so they
had accumulated drift under the 1% tolerance. Two examples worth following up: the marine habitat
and species tables render raw enum values (`reef`, `shallow`) where the model defines labels
(`Coral Reef`, `Shallow Reef (0-30 m)`), which is flagged for investigation and is NOT caused by the
wood commit since no rendering code changed, and the kopi editor no longer shows the
`$Object Details` panel header.

### D-145 — An empty dist/ revealed a lib entry-name mismatch with package.json

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-browser · active_

An earlier `npx vite build` in `core/blong-browser` emptied `dist/`, and the lib config emits
`blong-browser.js` and `storybook.js` while `package.json` references `dist/blong-browser.es.js` and
`dist/storybook.es.js`. The `.es.js` entry shims were re-created from the built entries to repair
the side effect. The underlying mismatch between `vite.config.ts` `lib.fileName` and `package.json`
was left as a todo.

### D-146 — The dark/light control became one borderless icon button

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-browser · active_

The segmented Light/Dark `SelectButton` was replaced by a single borderless sun/moon icon `Button`
with `text`, `rounded` and `severity="secondary"`, class `blong-theme-switcher__mode`, a 2.25rem
square hit area and a 1.1rem icon. A first pass removed the theme-family `Dropdown` too and the user
corrected it: the dropdown stays, only the dark/light control changes, so the earlier family-based
theme list decision still holds. Verified by `ThemeSwitcher.test.tsx`, 6 of 6, under
`npx vitest run`.

### D-147 — The mode icon shows the target mode and keeps the palette gate

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-browser · active_

Two implied choices in the switcher. The icon shows the mode the button switches TO — `pi pi-moon`
while light is active and `pi pi-sun` while dark is active — with `aria-label` and tooltip "Switch
to dark mode" and "Switch to light mode" translated through `useText`; reconsider if users expect
the icon to depict the current mode instead. The icon also renders only when the selected option has
BOTH variants, exactly as the old control did, so single-variant themes (vela, saga, arya) and the
dark-only Glass and Wood variants still show no toggle; a first-pass fallback that jumped to the
configured family's counterpart was dropped as out of scope once the dropdown was restored.

## Superseded

### D-076 — The first glass glare was one light sweep placed by projection

> _2026-09-06 · core/blong-browser · superseded_

The glass variant's glare was first built as a single top-left light sweep rather than strict line
collinearity: computing each panel's boundary from an exact global straight line (geometry divided
by each panel's axis length) saturated every lower same-column card to fully black at steep angles
of about 140 degrees. `src/components/Theme/glassReflection.ts` projected each panel's top-left
corner onto the shared light direction (sin/cos of `GLARE_ANGLE_DEG`, default 150), normalized over
the live panel stack and spread `--glare-shift` smoothly from 42% (nearest the light) to 12%
(farthest), while CSS reads `linear-gradient(var(--glare-angle, 150deg), ...)` so the JS angle and
the CSS gradient always agree. The knob is `GLARE_ANGLE_DEG` (90..180); verified live, toolbar 42%
down to habitat 12%, with the Form Inspector rail lit less (31% at the same row height as a 41%
card). The 250 ms interval plus resize/load refresh in `Theme.tsx` remains the trigger, because
async story content defeats MutationObserver and ResizeObserver in the Storybook iframe.

### D-077 — The visible glare edge is perpendicular to the CSS gradient axis

> _2026-09-06 · core/blong-browser · superseded_

Raising `GLARE_ANGLE_DEG` from 135 to 150 made the visible edge MORE horizontal, the opposite of the
request, because the user's "gradient line" is the visible light/dark EDGE and that edge is
perpendicular to the CSS `linear-gradient` axis: axis 150 degrees gives an edge of about 30 degrees,
axis 135 about 45, axis 90 is vertical and axis 103 is about 77 (steep). The 90..180 knob stays and
smaller means a more vertical edge. The symptom "tops align, bottoms wrong" meant parallel per-panel
edges placed by projection rather than collinear ones, so the fix was a strict single straight edge:
`shift_i = (edgeC − axis-projection of top-left) / axis span_i`, with `edgeC` taken from the
top-most anchor panel at `ANCHOR_FRACTION` (0.5). Every main-column card then landed on edge
constant 357.8 (toolbar 50, edit 66.3, taxonomy 53.4, reproduction 40.9, morphology 27.5, links
13%). A single steep edge can only cross one vertical column, so the far-right Form Inspector rail
and the last low card fell back to a top-left falloff (`FALLOFF_TOP` 0.4 to `FALLOFF_BOTTOM` 0.1)
instead of pure black, and the CSS fallback in `glass.css` (`var(--glare-angle, 103deg)`) must match
`GLARE_ANGLE_DEG`.
